Case Study: A Wheelchair Access Ramp

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

A city library installs a wheelchair access ramp so that visitors can reach the raised entrance safely. Accessibility guidelines fix a maximum angle that any ramp may make with the level ground, because a ramp that is too steep becomes dangerous to use. If a ramp climbs a vertical height h over a horizontal run r, the angle it makes with the ground is the principal value of the arctangent, θ=tan⁻¹ (h/r). Since both h and r are positive here, this angle is always acute. The main ramp rises 1 m over a run of √3 m, while a shorter service ramp rises 1 m over a run of 1 m. The surveyor records each angle exactly, and also works out the least horizontal run needed to keep a 1 m rise within the guideline limit.
